Q: Why does checkbox size change during transition? A:

I do not believe that there is a particular CSS property that is causing the rounding error. It seems to be a subpixel rounding problem that occurs during the process of animation. Depending on the zoom level, the layout will be recalculated in each frame, and the native checkbox may be rendered one pixel wider or smaller.

You may consider trying to get rid of the width: min-content property if you do not need it, or you could try to animate opacity and transform properties instead of the height. If that does not help, then it probably is just the rendering problem of the browser.

Q: AVPlayer Audio Reverse Scrubbing A:

AVPlayer isn't really designed for this use case.

Its primary goal is media playback, not sample-accurate transport. Even with different timePitchAlgorithm values or varying rate, AVPlayer is free to decode ahead, drop frames, buffer, and optimize playback however it sees fit. It does not expose decoded PCM or guarantee that the audio being rendered corresponds exactly to the current playhead position—especially during rapid scrubbing or reverse playback.

Reverse playback is another major limitation. While AVPlayer supports negative playback rates for some assets, it does not decode audio in reverse. In practice, reverse audio playback requires decoding the audio yourself and presenting the PCM samples in reverse order.

If you need all of the following:

  • sample-accurate audio during scrubbing,

  • correct audio regardless of scrub speed,

  • reverse audio when scrubbing backwards,

  • streamed assets,

then your current architecture (or something very similar) is the correct approach. Decode the audio into PCM and drive playback yourself using AVAudioEngine/AVAudioPlayerNode (or a lower-level Audio Unit if you need even tighter control).

Using an AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate so that both AVPlayer and your PCM cache consume the same network stream is actually a reasonable optimization if you still want AVPlayer to handle normal playback. It avoids maintaining two independent downloads while letting you build the PCM cache required for scrubbing.

So I don't think you've missed an obvious "vanilla" API. Apple doesn't provide a high-level API that combines:

  • streaming,

  • sample-accurate scrubbing,

  • reverse audio playback, and

  • seamless integration with AVPlayer.

Once you require sample-level control over what's being rendered, you're effectively outside of AVPlayer's design goals and into the territory of AVAudioEngine/Core Audio.

Q: How to get raw mouse XY data in VB6 A:

Note: The solution to my question in this answer is based on the very helpful comments of /u/GSerg.

This Answer focuses on the problem areas in the Question.

An alternative form of Answer would provide a full set of code.

Here are some (of many) Microsoft documents (focused on C and C++, not VB6) relating to the methods used:-

[Using Raw Input](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/using-raw-input?source=recommendations)

[Raw Input](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/raw-input?source=recommendations)

[RAWINPUT structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawinput)

[RAWINPUTHEADER structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawinputheader)

[RAWMOUSE structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-rawmouse)

The first issue is to correct the parameters in the First call to GetRawInputData putting ByVal 0& instead of vbNullString and setting cbSizeHeader=16 (the standard length of theRAWINPUTHEADER ).

cbSizeHeader=16
status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, ByVal 0&, pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

This will return the the value of 40(bytes) for pcbsize .

Then the pData array to receive the mouse data should be sized to 40 bytes,

Then in the second call to GetRawInputData the third parameter will be pData(0).

status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, pData(0), pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

The UDT type structure to receive the header and mouse data should be something like:-

'in Module...

Public Type RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA
    '------- header ---------
    dwType As Long
    dwSize As Long
    hDevice As Long
    wParam As Long 
    '-------- mouse data--------
    usFlags As Integer
    '-------------------------
    '... either 1 item:-
    'ulButtons As Long
    '... or 2 items:-
    usButtonFlags As Integer
    usButtonData As Integer
    '-------------------------
    ulRawButtons As Long
    lLastX As Long
    lLastY As Long
    ulExtraInformation As Long
End Type

' in Form code...
dim mouseData as RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA

Then the data can be memory-copied to the mouseData object.

            
'in Module...

Public Declare Sub CopyMemory Lib "kernel32" Alias "RtlMoveMemory" ( _
    ByRef Destination As Any, _
    ByRef Source As Any, _
    ByVal Length As Long)

'in Form code...

CopyMemory mouseData, pData(0), Len(mouseData) '..  Destination, Source, Length

Then the latest mouse position data can be accessed as mouseData.lLastX and mouseData.lLastY.

Note that instead of using copyMemory , the Second call to GetRawInputData can pass the mouse data directly to the mouseData array, thus:-

status = GetRawInputData(lParam, uiCommand, mouseData(0), pcbSize, cbSizeHeader)

Note that the UDT Type RAWINPUTWITHMOUSEDATA uses 38 bytes, in contrast to the 40 bytes for pcbsize returned by the First call to GetRawInputData . The difference is due to 2 extra bytes of padding being used (by Windows) in the latter to comply with memory alignment padding and packing rules. there may be some unresolved issues relating to this 2-byte difference.

Q: Manifest merger failed with multiple errors, see logs after migrating the project to android 16 A:

You can find out the issues in the Merged Manifest and then resolve them. To navigate to the Merged Manifest, follow the steps:

AndroidManifest.xml -> Merged Manifest tab from the bottom. There you will see any error in Red color. This way you will find your issue and will eventually solve it!
